item.title: Arsenal will only sell Gyokeres if this condition is met
item.description: Arsenal will only sell Gyokeres if this condition is met Viktor Gyokeres’ future at Arsenal remains uncertain as he continues to struggle to earn the confidence of manager Mikel Arteta and his teammates. The Swedish striker has yet to establish himself as the reliable attacking option the club expected when he arrived, raising questions about his long-term future at the Emirates Stadium. In midweek, Gyokeres produced a fantastic goal for Arsenal in the Champions League , demonstrating that he remains capable of moments of brilliance, as he regularly did during his time at Sporting Club. His performance offered a reminder of the quality he possesses and the contribution he can still make to the team. However, producing occasional moments of quality will not be enough to secure his position in the starting line-up. He needs to deliver consistently and demonstrate that he can be trusted to lead Arsenal’s attack. So far, that consistency has been missing from his performances. Arsenal consider their options over Gyokeres Gyokeres has struggled to demonstrate the consistency required to become Arsenal’s leading striker. Although the club could consider selling him if an attractive offer arrives, they are not prepared to sanction his departure without carefully considering their options. According to Football Insider , Arsenal would ideally like to secure a top replacement for the Swedish forward before agreeing to let him leave. The report suggests that the Gunners still consider him an important member of their squad and would therefore want to ensure they have another attacking option ready before approving a transfer. This approach indicates that Arsenal are not necessarily looking to force Gyokeres out of the club. Instead, they appear to be preparing for different possibilities while ensuring that their attacking options remain strong enough to compete. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Gyokeres’ future depends on Arsenal’s recruitment Gyokeres reportedly wants to remain at Arsenal, but his future is not entirely in his own hands. His performances over the coming period could influence the club’s thinking, although recruitment decisions will also play an important role. If Arsenal identify and secure a replacement capable of providing more goals, they could become more willing to consider offers for the Swede. For now, his position remains uncertain, with the club seemingly determined to protect its attacking strength before making any significant decision about his future. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Patriots defense preparing for every quarterback possibility with Chargers
item.description: The New England Patriots are not the only team facing quarterback questions heading into Week 12. The Los Angeles Chargers, their opponent on Sunday, are in the same boat. Starting QB Justin Herbert remains in concussion protocol and was a no-show at practice both Wednesday and Thursday. With his status in question, backup D.J. Uiagalelei might be elevated into the starting role. Given that uncertainty, the Patriots defense is faced with a question: who to prepare for? “That’s a question that gets asked a lot: ‘You don’t know if a quarterback’s going to play or not, do you prepare for all of them?’ It’s lot about us,” defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr explained earlier this week. “Obviously, we know a lot more about Herbert’s play style than the next two guys, D.J. and Jake [Browning], if they make Jake active. But they are aware of their play styles. Obviously, there’s a lot more tape of Herbert, but everybody’s aware of the contingency plans. We went over that again [Wednesday], the contingency plans if we get news if something else changes.” Kuhr likened the situation to preparing for Denver Broncos backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham ahead of last year’s AFC Championship Game. That contest came two weeks after New England’s most recent meeting with Herbert, whose offense was held to three points in the wild card round. Uiagalelei was inactive as a member of the Chargers’ practice squad that day. Now, 10 months later, he is in line to potentially get his first career start and add to a résumé consisting of a mere 21 regular season snaps — all of them in a loss to the Texans earlier this season — as well as two pass completions on seven attempts for 24 yards and a touchdown. Despite the limited output so far, the Patriots have to familiarize themselves with the 25-year-old former undrafted free agent. And in the process of doing so, they have seen some differences to Los Angeles’ regular starter. “Strong arm. I would say more from the pocket than Herbert,” Kuhr said about his game. “Obviously, some inexperience. But he made some plays in college; obviously, he’s made a roster. So, I would say he’s a professional, he’s going to take advantage of his opportunity just like every backup quarterback does.”

item.title: Dolphins counting on rookies to push through NFL's 'rookie wall'
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS — It's Week 12 in the NFL and Kadyn Proctor of the Miami Dolphins is one of the many rookies who played 12 regular-season college games last year. Now, Proctor had three more games because Alabama always plays extra games. But the point here is that all NFL rookies hit the proverbial "rookie wall" at some point in late November or December. "I feel wonderful," Proctor said this week. "I've been telling my teammates. They've informed me about the rookie wall. I said I'm not going to hit it." The Dolphins (1-9) host the Jets (3-8) on Sunday, Nov. 29 at Hard Rock Stadium. And no team in the NFL has relied more on rookies than the Dolphins this season. "The wall's a concern for a big part of our team that are rookies and that are playing a lot of snaps, right?" Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said. "So we are very aware of that." No NFL team has more rookie starts than the Dolphins, with 66. The Browns have 43. The Giants have 29. "I understand our team and I understand that we have seven games left and the college season has one more and it's not even really that," Hafley said. "It's just these guys have not stopped since their playoff game or bowl game and then Combine and then pro days and then rookie mini camp, OTAs and then they finally caught a breath, so they haven't stopped for two years. So it's very real, right? So it's recovery, it's sleep, it's us doing a really good job of not just the physical part, but the mental fatigue is very, very real." Key Dolphins rookies include: OL Kadyn Proctor , CB Chris Johnson , LB Jacob Rodriguez , WR Caleb Douglas , TE Will Kacmarek and S Michael Taaffe . The Dolphins drafted 13 rookies. And they've added six more since the season began. One draft pick has been cut. One is on injured reserve. Three are on practice squad. Miami Dolphins currently have 14 rostered rookies On the one hand, young Dolphins are improving and learning the pro game and schemes. On the other hand, a team with an average age of 25.6 — 25.6! — has a lot to learn. "With a young team, it's been a little bit slower, but they're really starting to pick it up," Hafley said. As for this infamous "rookie wall?" "I've got to take care of my body and know I still have a whole half of the season to play," said Johnson, the cornerback. "And like you said, I've heard about it from multiple teammates. But I feel like it is what it is. I love playing football, so I'm going to just hopefully keep my body healthy for as long as possible and continue playing." Hard-hitting rookie fullback DJ Herman said: "Hot tubs and cold tubs and the sauna, make sure my body's warm, more stretching. So after multiple weeks of just kind of getting into a groove and making sure that what works and what doesn't, you kind of just get a basis of like, all right, this works and this doesn't." item.title: OFFICIAL: Brahim Díaz signs Real Madrid contract extension
item.description: Real Madrid have announced the extension of Brahim Díaz’s contract, which will now keep him at the club at least until the summer of 2031. Per Realmadrid.com Real Madrid and Brahim Díaz have agreed to a contract extension that ties the player to the club through June 30, 2031. Mr. Díaz arrived at Real Madrid in 2019 at the age of 19. In six seasons with the club, he has appeared in 173 matches and won seven titles: one Champions League, one Club World Cup, one UEFA Super Cup, two league titles and two Spanish Super Cups. An international for Morocco, he has earned 36 caps and scored 15 goals for his national team, and finished as the top scorer at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. Brahim has accepted his role as a bench player and he’s been serviceable in the minutes he’s played, so this extension makes sense for the two sides.

item.description: Tyson Fury has reportedly been medically cleared to box Anthony Joshua , after confusion around a possible schizophrenia diagnosis. Fury is scheduled to face his fellow British heavyweight on 11 December , as the pair headline at Cardiff’s Principallity stadium in a fight years in the making. However, the bout appeared to be under threat this week, as quotes from Tyson Fury – a new Netflix documentary – did the rounds. The quotes saw Fury’s wife Paris suggesting that the boxer was once diagnosed with schizophrenia. Tyson Fury in 2026 (PA) That prompted Robert Smith, general secretary of the British Boxing Board of Control (BBBofC), to tell the BBC: “We are in the process of dealing with the matter, but if there are any medical issues we wouldn’t let anyone box. It doesn’t matter if it’s Tyson Fury or not, it could be anybody. I’m fairly confident he will be absolutely fine. We’re dealing with it now and we’ll have an answer very shortly.” Paris soon released a statement that read : “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. “Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love. I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.” Meanwhile, Netflix said: “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.” The film was released on Friday, and the scene in question had been reported on earlier this week, following preview screenings earlier in November . Fury will finally face Anthony Joshua on 11 December (PA Wire) Friday also brought a report from journalist Gareth A Davies, who tweeted: “Tyson Fury’s medicals were all cleared by the Boxing Board on Thursday evening. item.title: Leipzig only open to January sale of Antonio Nusa for an irresistible offer
item.description: Leipzig only open to January sale of Antonio Nusa for an irresistible offer RB Leipzig will only consider sell Antonio Nusa in January if an irresistible offer arrives for the winger. Nusa is attracting interest from Europe's biggest clubs after a brilliant start to the season in Leipzig. The 21-year-old has five goals and seven assists in 10 Bundesliga appearances, and has scored three times in the Champions League. That return includes a double against Lens in midweek. His influence for Norway is also increasing. Nusa was on target against Wales during November's international break and has now scored 10 goals in 36 caps. He's become an important figure for Ståle Solbakken's side, alongside Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard. Arsenal have made Nusa a top target as the Gunners look to sign a left-winger, while Paris Saint-Germain have also shortlisted the Norwegian. PSG want to sign a winger in January, following season-ending ACL injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue. Bayern Munich are also monitoring his performances this season. Leipzig are set to hold firm until the summer, report Sky Germany , unless the German side receives an offer above €100m (£83.5m). Leipzig need to recoup around €100m in the upcoming transfer windows and would only consider a mid-season sale, should that offer arrive. The Bundesliga side want Nusa to remain and help their bid for Champions League qualification, before his future is reassessed in the summer. Leipzig expect him to stay until at least the end of the season.

item.title: How tight ends give Delaware football more ways to attack defenses
item.description: At certain times and places, the tight end has been an endangered species on college football fields. It’s not uncommon to see an offense line up without a tight end, a position that requires sturdy blocking ability plus the elusiveness and dexterity to catch passes. The Air Raid and Run-and-Shoot offenses are among those that typically don’t employ someone at that position. Spread offenses can go with or without them, but Delaware coach Ryan Carty has found value in having tight ends in is schemes. It was never more obvious than in Delaware’s Nov. 21 Conference USA game at New Mexico State. Tight ends caught all five of Nick Minicucci’s touchdown passes in the 42-30 victory, which was Delaware’s sixth of the season and made the Blue Hens bowl eligible. “It was a great day for the tight ends,” sophomore tight end Scott Moore said. “Five touchdowns for a room, it’s great. We love that the tight ends got so much love that game . . . We just happen to be open. We’re not always the first option.” Moore snared three of those TD passes, from 19 yards in the second quarter, 9 yards in the third quarter and a nifty 20-yarder when it appeared Minicucci was running before flipping the ball over approaching defenders to the wide-open Moore. Dover High grad Elijah Sessoms caught a 4-yarder for Delaware’s first TD and Josh Humes, the transfer from Coastal Carolina, grabbed a 44-yarder in the fourth quarter. The Blue Hens (6-5 overall, 4-3 CUSA) will likely need similar contributions when Jacksonville State (8-3, 6-1) visits Delaware Stadium in the regular-season Nov. 28. Kickoff is at 3:30 p.m. with the CBS Sports Network televising. “I think the biggest thing for us offensively, the way we see it,” Carty said, “is we want to have the ability to, as much as we can, stay in 11 personnel -- one tight end, three receivers, one running back -- so that we can move down the field without changing personnel as much. We can do whatever we need out of that.” When Carty was offensive coordinator at Sam Houston from 2018-21, there were times he used tight ends less in his spread offense. That was more, he said, because of the personnel he had, adding many of the Texas high schools from which Sam Houston recruited ran Air Raid offenses and, therefore, didn’t produce as many tight end prospects. “When you take a tight end off the field,” Carty said, “you kind of limit a lot of the things that you can do in the run game. You can't add that extra hat [for blocking] as well. You also limit what you can do in the protection game.” Delaware will also sometimes line up in 12 personnel groupings – one running back and two tight ends. Moore, who played high school football in Kansas in a Delaware Wing-T offense, appreciates the value Delaware puts on the position. item.title: “A lot of positives” – Thomas Frank reacts to his first win in charge of Crystal Palace
item.description: “A lot of positives” – Thomas Frank reacts to his first win in charge of Crystal Palace Crystal Palace 2-1 Real Sociedad, Thomas Frank Targets Turning Point After First Win Thomas Frank has been in the job for two matches and already has something Crystal Palace badly needed, a win. The 2-1 victory over Real Sociedad does not change Palace being bottom of the Premier League, but it does give the new manager a result he can point to and, more importantly, a response from his players. Palace were behind in the second half after Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr scored for Sociedad. From there, the game shifted. Jon Martin picked up a second yellow card, Sociedad went down to 10 men, and Palace finally took control of the situation. Jean-Philippe Mateta equalised from the penalty spot, then Dwight McNeil came off the bench to score the winner. Photo IMAGO Thomas Frank Finds Early Lift Frank was clear about what mattered. “In the second half I felt we kept the ball much better,” Frank said after his side’s victory on Thursday. “What I really liked was the belief from the players. It is so important to keep doing the right things and keep believing.” That belief was required because Palace still made life harder for themselves. They gave the ball away too cheaply, offered Sociedad chances and nearly threw away the win late on. Dean Henderson had to produce a last-gasp save after Yeremy Pino saw Palace’s second penalty of the night saved. Crystal Palace Still Short on Confidence Frank did not pretend everything was fixed. “We should just control that game. But we probably don’t have the confidence right now.” That is the truth of Palace’s current state. One win helps, but confidence is not restored by one decent half against 10 men. Hull Test Carries Real Weight Frank knows that as well. Asked if this could be a turning point, he said: “I think it could be. item.description: Motorsport photo With F1 close to signing off on the overarching tenets of its 2030 return to V8 power units, some of its leading drivers have fleshed out ideas of how to make those into a compelling product. F1 is set to move to all-new turbo V8 engines in 2030, with a smaller electric unit of up to 200kW and sustainable fuel. That should make engines simpler, cheaper and lighter, and therefore reduce the reliance on energy from the battery compared to today's oft-criticised formula. By signing off the V8 move at the next FIA World Motor Sport Council gathering in Shanghai on 12 December, F1 and the FIA are giving themselves time to properly flesh out the chassis and aerodynamic regulations that should work in unison with the V8 power units to produce a better on-track show. Last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix has given the series some food for though about what it really wants from its next rules cycle. At the Las Vegas street circuit, F1 delivered an absorbing spectacle featuring a record 35 lead changes, aided by a combination of the powerful slipstreaming effect and the boost mode from the power unit, which led to so-called yo-yo racing as the lead car often ended up a sitting duck on the straight. While there was debate on whether that's the kind of show F1 wants to see more of, or whether Vegas was too artificial for its own good, it further highlighted the importance of developing a combination of power unit parameters and aerodynamics overtaking aids that can be fine-tuned on a race-to-race basis to deliver a solid spectacle without making overtaking too trivial either. It prompted Williams driver and Grand Prix Drivers' Association director Carlos Sainz to come up with an intriguing idea on how to tune a DRS-like overtaking system for 2030, suggesting a straightline boost that aids chasing drivers coming right out of the corners. item.title: Hamilton Is Two Races From Beating Leclerc on Points, Poles and Podiums—a First
item.description: Lewis Hamilton leads Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc on points, Grand Prix podiums and poles with two races left in the 2026 Formula 1 season. If he holds on in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, he will be the first teammate to finish a full season ahead of Leclerc on all three, a point Autosport made this week. Our own check of every season Leclerc has raced in F1 backs it up. Where the Ferrari Teammates Stand After Las Vegas After 21 rounds, Hamilton has 267 points to Leclerc’s 250, in the official standings . Those totals include sprint points. On Grand Prix podiums, it’s seven to six. Hamilton’s came in China, Canada, Monaco, Barcelona, Britain, Bahrain and Mexico, and one of them was a win in Barcelona. Leclerc’s came in Australia, Japan, Britain, Belgium, Singapore and Austin, with his win at Silverstone. Sprint podiums aren’t in that count. Add them, and it’s level at 10 each: Hamilton has three sprint podiums and Leclerc four, by our count of the official results. The pole count is the thinnest margin: one to none. Hamilton took his first Ferrari pole in Mexico City, by 0.009 seconds from George Russell, with Leclerc third. It would be a big turnaround from 2025, Hamilton’s first year in red. Leclerc beat him 242 points to 156 that season and took seven Grand Prix podiums, while Hamilton didn’t get one. Las Vegas added to the gap. On the Strip, Leclerc’s late lunge at Turn 7 spun Hamilton out of sixth and earned Leclerc a 10-second penalty. Hamilton fought back to seventh, while Leclerc dropped to 10th. Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas GP. Image Credit: Scuderia Ferrari / X Why No Leclerc Teammate Has Done It Before Leclerc has had four full-time teammates since his debut with Sauber in 2018. We counted a teammate as beating him only when they finished a season strictly ahead on all three: championship points, Grand Prix podiums and poles. Marcus Ericsson, his Sauber teammate in 2018, scored nine points to Leclerc’s 39, and neither took a podium or a pole. At Ferrari, Sebastian Vettel trailed him on all three in 2019, then on points and podiums in 2020, a year when neither Ferrari took a pole. Carlos Sainz came closest. In 2021, he beat Leclerc 164.5 points to 159 and four Grand Prix podiums to one, but Leclerc took two poles to Sainz’s none. Leclerc then led Sainz on all three from 2022 to 2024, and Hamilton on all three in 2025. That makes 2026 Hamilton’s to lose. Leclerc can still stop it with a single pole, by finishing on the podium more often than Hamilton in the last two races, or by outscoring him by 17 points or more. Any fight will happen under a warning from the top. Team principal Fred Vasseur was blunt about the Vegas contact after the race, Autosport reported . “It’s unacceptable. It’s a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors, the same speech as after Mexico.”

item.title: New Wayne Gretzky Documentary Premieres Today, Revisiting The Stick That Changed Hockey
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Wayne Gretzky had already won four Stanley Cups and nine Hart Trophies, including eight consecutively, by the time he made one of the most influential equipment changes in hockey history. In 1990, entering his third season with the Los Angeles Kings, Gretzky ditched the wooden Titan stick he’d used throughout much of his NHL career in favor of a two-piece aluminum stick manufactured by Easton. More than three decades later, the NHL is revisiting that decision in a 24-minute documentary titled The Stick That Changed the Game , scheduled to premiere today at 11 a.m. ET on the league’s YouTube channel. Gretzky wasn’t the first hockey player to use an aluminum stick, but there wasn’t a player on the planet who could do more for the popularity of a piece of hockey equipment. He was coming off a 142-point season with the Kings, and the attention he’d brought to hockey in Southern California made him an ideal candidate to introduce a relatively unconventional product to the masses. According to NHL.com’s Dave Stubbs , Gretzky preferred an unusually stiff shaft and a moderate blade curve. Achieving that level of stiffness with a wooden stick meant carrying some extra weight, something Gretzky generally tried to avoid with his equipment. Easton was able to develop an aluminum model that catered to his preferences. Gretzky’s agent, Mike Barnett, also wanted the stick to be easily recognizable. Easton polished the aluminum shaft to give it the shiny silver appearance that became synonymous with Gretzky’s years in Los Angeles, allowing fans watching on television to immediately recognize that the greatest player in the world was using something different. Gretzky scored twice in the Kings’ season-opening victory over the New York Islanders on Oct. 4, 1990, and went on to register 163 points in 78 games that season, winning his ninth career Art Ross Trophy. The documentary also features current NHL players getting their hands on Gretzky’s old stick. It weighs 614 grams, compared to the 359-gram modern composite stick used for comparison in the film. That’s a pretty substantial difference for players who grew up using composite sticks, especially considering Gretzky’s Easton was designed with weight reduction in mind. Gretzky himself eventually went back to using a wooden stick toward the end of his career with the New York Rangers after investing in the Hespeler hockey equipment company. There are generations of hockey players who have never had to buy a replacement blade, heat the end of a shaft or spend an afternoon trying to get a stubborn wooden plug out of a broken stick. For anyone who grew up doing those things, Friday’s documentary should be a fun watch. For anyone who didn’t, it might be equally entertaining and informative. item.title: Dan Evans to compete in controversial Gazprom-backed exhibition tournament
item.description: Retired British tennis player Dan Evans is in the line-up for a highly controversial exhibition tournament which is sponsored by Russian energy giant Gazprom . Gazprom is majority state-owned and has been sanctioned by the UK government for its role in funding Russia’s war in Ukraine, with a 2025 statement saying its profits were “lining Putin’s war chest and facilitating the war”. The company sponsors the annual Northern Palmyra Trophies exhibition, which is held this year from 27-29 November in St Petersburg and features 12 current or former tennis players. Russia has not held any official ATP or WTA Tour events since the invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and Russian and Belarusian players cannot represent their country, instead competing as neutral athletes. However, exhibitions are not covered by the rules governing Tour events and players are free to play in such tournaments on Russian soil. Evans, who retired at Wimbledon this year, has not commented on his decision to take part in the event. The Northern Palmyra Trophies sees two teams face off in a mix of singles and doubles matches, with Evans drawn against world No 11, Russia’s Diana Shnaider, in a Battle of the Sexes-style clash. Frenchmen Adrian Mannarino and Corentin Moutet are also in the line-up, which primarily consists of Russian or Russian-born players. Top-100 players Anastasia Potapova , Kamilla Rakhimova, and Yulia Putintseva , who were all born in Russia, are competing, as is the retired former world No 13 Elena Vesnina . Potapova and Rakhimova have both switched nationality since the war began, with the former now representing Austria and the latter Uzbekistan. Putintseva has represented Kazakhstan since 2012. Russian 17-year-old Anna Pushkareva, compatriot Karen Khachanov , retired Serbian player Jakno Tipsarevic and Kazakhstan’s Alexander Bublik complete the line-up. Former US Open champion Daniil Medvedev competed last year but is absent for 2026. The Netherlands’ Tallon Griekspoor, who is in a relationship with Potapova, sparked a diplomatic incident when he decided to play in last year’s tournament. Dutch Foreign Minister David van Weel issued a public statement urging him to withdraw, to no avail: “It is not forbidden to participate in tournaments in Russia, but I appeal to him not to do so where possible and to look at the moral aspects.” The Russian embassy said it was “deeply concerned” by the “pressure” put on Griekspoor.

item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
